title: Coherent derived Hom into a finite-injective-dimension coherent complex
statement: Let $A$ be a commutative Noetherian ring [def-weil-pbc-noetherian-ring], and let $K,L\in D(A)$ [def-weil-abstract-derived-category]. Assume that every cohomology module of $K$ and of $L$ is finitely generated over $A$ [def-weil-finitely-generated-module], without requiring $K$ to be bounded in either direction. If $L$ is isomorphic in $D(A)$ to a bounded complex of injective $A$-modules [def-sp-injective-resolutions], then every cohomology module of $R\operatorname{Hom}_A(K,L)$ [def-pur-derived-internal-hom] is finitely generated over $A$.

source.place: Tag 0G4H, lemma-finite-ext-into-bounded-injective; finite injective dimension expanded by more-algebra.tex Tag 0A5S, definition-injective-dimension.

proof.text: Choose a bounded injective complex $I$ representing $L$, supported in $[a,b]$, and a complex $P$ representing $K$. The derived isomorphisms of [lem-trf-bounded-injective-rhom-model-support] compute $R\operatorname{Hom}_A(QM,L)$ by $Q\operatorname{Hom}_A^\bullet(M,I)$, naturally in $M$; compose with $QI\cong L$. All maps and cohomology comparisons retain the $A$-action.

source.place: Tag 0G4H, lemma-finite-ext-into-bounded-injective, proof: bounded injective computation and truncation comparison, expanded at the complex level.

proof.text: Fix $i\in\mathbf Z$ and set $n=b-i+1$. Let $T=\tau_{\leq n}P$ and $C=P/T$. Thus $T^q=P^q$ for $q<n$, $T^n=\ker d_P^n$, and $T^q=0$ for $q>n$. Consequently $C^q=0$ for $q<n$ and $0\to T\to P\to C\to0$ is degreewise short exact. By [lem-weil-pbc-truncation-cohomology], $H^q(T)\cong H^q(K)$ for $q\leq n$ and $H^q(T)=0$ above $n$, so all its cohomology is finite.

source.place: Tag 0G4H, lemma-finite-ext-into-bounded-injective, proof: bounded injective computation and truncation comparison, expanded at the complex level.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-bounded-injective-total-hom-exact] to $0\to T\to P\to C\to0$ and the chosen $I$. This gives the degreewise short exact sequence $0\to\operatorname{Hom}_A^\bullet(C,I)\to\operatorname{Hom}_A^\bullet(P,I)\to\operatorname{Hom}_A^\bullet(T,I)\to0$ of complexes of $A$-modules.

source.place: Tag 0G4H, lemma-finite-ext-into-bounded-injective, proof: bounded injective computation and truncation comparison, expanded at the complex level.

proof.text: The support clause of [lem-trf-bounded-injective-rhom-model-support], applied to $C^q=0$ for $q<n$, makes $\operatorname{Hom}_A^r(C,I)=0$ for $r>b-n=i-1$. In particular its cohomology in degrees $i$ and $i+1$ vanishes. The long exact sequence [lem-weil-pbc-complex-ses-homology-long-exact] of Step 3 therefore makes $H^i\operatorname{Hom}_A^\bullet(P,I)\to H^i\operatorname{Hom}_A^\bullet(T,I)$ an $A$-linear isomorphism. Step 1 identifies these modules with $H^iR\operatorname{Hom}_A(K,L)$ and $H^iR\operatorname{Hom}_A(QT,L)$.

source.place: Tag 0G4H, lemma-finite-ext-into-bounded-injective, proof: bounded injective computation and truncation comparison, expanded at the complex level.

proof.text: Apply [lem-trf-bounded-above-coherent-rhom] to $QT,L$ with upper bound $u=n$ and lower bound $v=a$. Step 2 supplies bounded-above finite cohomology of $QT$; the representative $I$ gives $H^q(L)=0$ for $q<a$, and $L$ has finite cohomology by hypothesis. Hence $H^iR\operatorname{Hom}_A(QT,L)$ is finitely generated. The isomorphism of Step 4 transfers finite generation to $H^iR\operatorname{Hom}_A(K,L)$. This holds for every $i$ without a bound on $K$.

source.place: Tag 0D0C, lemma-coherent-internal-hom, proof: the explicitly stated algebra problem for L in D^+_Coh(A) and K in D^-_Coh(A), with its lower bound v-u from the displayed bounded spectral sequences.
